subject: anthropology
topicTitle: Tribal Society in India, Classification, Problems, Constitutional Safeguards

ncertReference.book: Indian Tribal Anthropology (Class XII Curriculum / CBSE)
ncertReference.chapter: Unit IV: Tribal Society in India: Profile and Safeguards

thirtySecondSummary: Tribal populations (Scheduled Tribes / Adivasis) comprise 8.6% of India's population (2011 Census, 104.3 million), characterized by primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shy contact with larger society, and economic backwardness (Lokur Committee criteria, 1965).

Geographic distribution spans 5 major zones: North-Eastern (Nagas, Mizo, Khasi), Central / Middle India (Santhal, Munda, Oraon, Gond, Bhil - largest tribal demographic), Southern (Toda, Kadar, Chenchu, Irula), Western (Bhil, Mina), and Island Zone (Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa, Sentinelese, Shompen).

Linguistic classifications encompass 4 major language families: Austro-Asiatic (Mundari, Santhali, Khasi), Tibeto-Burman (Bodo, Garo, Naga), Dravidian (Gondi, Kurukh, Kui), and Indo-Aryan (Bhil, Halbi).

Major developmental and socio-economic problems include Land alienation, Usurious indebtedness, Shifting cultivation (Jhum), Forest rights displacement, Mining-induced displacement, Malnutrition, and Educational lag.

Constitutional safeguards provide robust protection: Fifth Schedule (Scheduled Areas in 10 states, Tribes Advisory Council), Sixth Schedule (Autonomous District Councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram), PESA Act 1996 (Gram Sabha empowerment), Forest Rights Act (FRA 2006), and Article 338A (National Commission for Scheduled Tribes - NCST).

coreConcepts.title: Demographic Profile, Criteria and Geographic Classification
coreConcepts.explanation:
Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes as communities deemed under Article 342. The Lokur Committee (1965) established 5 canonical criteria:
1. Indications of primitive traits.
2. Distinctive culture.
3. Geographical isolation.
4. Shyness of contact with the community at large.
5. General backwardness.
Geographic Classification (L.P. Vidyarthi & B.S. Guha):
1. North-Eastern Zone: Assam, Arunachal, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya. Tribes: Naga, Kuki, Mizo, Garo, Khasi. Speak Tibeto-Burman & Austro-Asiatic; high literacy.
2. Central / Middle India Zone: West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, MP, Chhattisgarh. Largest tribal concentration (> 55% of total STs). Tribes: Gond, Bhil, Santhal, Munda, Oraon, Ho. Rich mineral belt; severely afflicted by displacement.
3. Southern Zone: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, AP, Telangana. Tribes: Toda, Kota, Irula, Kadar, Chenchu, Kurumba. Small populations, pastoralism/foraging.
4. Western Zone: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra. Tribes: Bhil, Mina, Warli, Katkari.
5. Island Zone: Andaman & Nicobar. Negrito hunter-gatherers (Jarawa, Onge, Sentinelese, Great Andamanese) and Mongoloid (Nicobarese, Shompen).
keyTakeaways: ST Population: 8.6% of India (2011 Census); Bhil is the largest tribe, followed by Gond.
Lokur Committee (1965): 5 criteria for ST scheduling.
Island Zone Negrito tribes: Sentinelese, Jarawa, Onge (PVTGs under extreme protection).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Indian Tribal Anthropology Class XII, Section 4.1 & 4.2, pp. 150-164.

coreConcepts.title: Linguistic and Economic Typology of Indian Tribes
coreConcepts.explanation:
1. Linguistic Classification:
- Austro-Asiatic Family: Mon-Khmer branch (Khasi, Jaintia of Meghalaya, Nicobarese) and Munda branch (Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Birhor, Kharia).
- Tibeto-Burman Family: Spoken across Himalayan and North-Eastern tribes (Bodo, Garo, Mikir, Ao Naga, Angami Naga, Mizo, Lepcha).
- Dravidian Family: Gondi (Gonds), Kurukh/Oraon (Oraons), Malto (Rajmahal hills), Kui/Kuvi (Khonds), Toda, Kadar, Chenchu.
- Indo-Aryan Family: Bhili (Bhils), Halbi (Bastar), Khandeshi.
2. Economic Typologies (L.P. Vidyarthi):
- Hunting-Gathering / Foraging: Birhor (Jharkhand), Chenchu (AP), Kadar (Kerala), Jarawa (Andamans).
- Shifting Cultivation (Jhum / Podu / Bewar / Dahiya): Slash-and-burn farming on hill slopes (Nagas, Baiga, Maria Gond, Khond).
- Settled Agriculture: Santhal, Munda, Oraon, Gond, Bhil, Mina.
- Pastoralism: Gujjars and Bakarwals (transhumant pastoralists of J&K/Himachal), Toda (buffalo pastoralists of Nilgiris).
- Simple Artisans: Asur and Agaria (traditional iron smelters), Mahali (basket makers), Chick Baraik (weavers).
keyTakeaways: Austro-Asiatic: Santhali, Mundari (Munda branch) + Khasi (Mon-Khmer branch).
Dravidian tribal tongues: Gondi and Kurukh (Oraon).
Economic types: Birhor (foragers), Baiga (shifting jhum), Toda (buffalo pastoralists), Asur (iron smelters).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Indian Tribal Anthropology Class XII, Section 4.3, pp. 166-176.

coreConcepts.title: Major Tribal Problems and Constitutional Safeguards
coreConcepts.explanation:
1. Core Tribal Dilemmas:
- Land Alienation: Transfer of fertile tribal land to non-tribal money lenders and corporations.
- Indebtedness & Bonded Labor: Usurious interest rates charged by Mahajans/Sahukars.
- Shifting Cultivation (Jhum): Soil erosion, deforestation, pressure to assimilate into settled agriculture.
- Developmental Displacement: Hydel projects, coal mining, and industrial corridors displacing millions without adequate rehabilitation ('refugees of development').
2. Constitutional Safeguards:
- Protective Provisions: Article 15(4) & 16(4) (Reservations in education and public employment); Article 23 (prohibiting bonded labor/human trafficking); Article 244(1) (Administration of Scheduled Areas).
- Fifth Schedule: Applies to 10 states (Andhra, Telangana, Odisha, Jharkhand, MP, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, HP). Governor has legislative powers to amend acts; mandates a 'Tribes Advisory Council' (TAC).
- Sixth Schedule: Applies to 4 North-Eastern states (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram). Creates 'Autonomous District Councils' (ADCs) with legislative, executive, and judicial autonomy.
- Article 338A: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST, 89th Amendment 2003).
- PESA Act 1996: Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act empowers Gram Sabhas with ownership of Minor Forest Produce (MFP), prevention of land alienation, and mandatory consultation before land acquisition.
- Forest Rights Act (FRA 2006): Recognizes Individual and Community Forest Rights for STs and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (OTFDs).
keyTakeaways: Fifth Schedule (10 states, TAC, Governor's power) vs Sixth Schedule (AMTM: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram; ADCs).
PESA Act 1996: Empowers Gram Sabha over minor forest produce and development projects.
FRA 2006: Historical restoration of forest land and community grazing rights.
Article 338A: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Indian Tribal Anthropology Class XII, Section 4.4, pp. 178-191.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Fifth Schedule: 10 States | Sixth Schedule: AMTM (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram)
keyFacts.explanation: Fifth Schedule relies on Tribes Advisory Councils; Sixth Schedule creates constitutionally autonomous District and Regional Councils.
keyFacts.examTip: CUET regularly tests which 4 states are covered under the Sixth Schedule.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 | Dilip Singh Bhuria Committee
keyFacts.explanation: Extended grassroots local democracy to 5th Schedule areas, enshrining Gram Sabha authority over land, water, minerals, and minor forest produce.
keyFacts.examTip: Bhuria Committee recommendations led to the enactment of PESA 1996.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Formulated the 5 official criteria for identifying Scheduled Tribes in India
keyFacts.explanation: Primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographic isolation, shyness of contact, and backwardness.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: 75 identified tribal groups across 18 States and 1 UT (Dhebar Commission 1973)
keyFacts.explanation: Characterized by pre-agricultural level of technology, declining or stagnant population, extremely low literacy, and subsistence economy.
keyFacts.examTip: Highest number of PVTG groups reside in Odisha (13 groups).

workedExamples.question: Which four North-Eastern states are constitutionally governed under the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, providing for Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)?

options.text: Assam, Nagaland, Manipur, and Arunachal Pradesh

solutionSteps: Step 1: Recall the constitutional mandate of the Sixth Schedule under Articles 244(2) and 275(1).
Step 3: A = Assam, M = Meghalaya, T = Tripura, M = Mizoram.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: The 'AMTM' states under the Sixth Schedule are tested without fail across both Anthropology and Political Science exams.

workedExamples.question: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA), 1996 was enacted based on the recommendations of which expert committee?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Focus on the key legislation: PESA Act of 1996 extending self-governance to Fifth Schedule areas.
Step 2: The Government of India constituted the committee headed by Dilip Singh Bhuria (1994-95).
Step 3: Its historic report led directly to the passage of PESA, enshrining Gram Sabha supremacy.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: Distinguish: Lokur Committee = Criteria for scheduling STs (1965); Bhuria Committee = PESA (1995); Dhebar Commission = PVTGs (1973).

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: Match Santhali, Khasi, Gondi, and Bodo with Munda, Mon-Khmer, Dravidian, and Tibeto-Burman language families.
howCuetAsks.strategy: Remember: Santhali = Munda (Austro-Asiatic); Khasi = Mon-Khmer; Gondi = Dravidian; Bodo = Tibeto-Burman.

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: Under which Schedule of the Constitution is a 'Tribes Advisory Council' (TAC) mandatorily constituted?

commonTraps.whyItTraps: Khasi people live in Meghalaya surrounded by Tibeto-Burman speakers, but linguistically Khasi belongs to the Mon-Khmer branch of the Austro-Asiatic family.

commonTraps.trap: Thinking Gondi belongs to the Austro-Asiatic or Indo-Aryan family.
commonTraps.whyItTraps: Gonds live in Central India, but their ancestral language (Gondi) is Dravidian.
commonTraps.howToAvoid: Gondi and Kurukh (Oraon) are Central Indian Dravidian languages.

mnemonics.mnemonic: A-M-T-M = All Men Trust Mothers (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram)
mnemonics.meaning: The 4 states under Sixth Schedule Autonomous District Councils.
mnemonics.application: Directly solves Sixth Schedule state list questions.

practiceQuestions.question: According to the 2011 Census of India, Scheduled Tribes constitute approximately what percentage of the total Indian population?
practiceQuestions.explanation: As per the 2011 Census, the Scheduled Tribe population stands at 104.3 million, constituting 8.6% of the country's total population.

practiceQuestions.question: The Khasi language spoken in Meghalaya belongs to which linguistic family and branch?

options.text: Mon-Khmer branch of the Austro-Asiatic family

practiceQuestions.explanation: Khasi belongs to the Mon-Khmer branch of the Austro-Asiatic language family, sharing affinities with Nicobarese and Southeast Asian tongues.

practiceQuestions.question: Under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution of India, which body must be constituted in each state having Scheduled Areas to advise on tribal welfare?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Fifth Schedule mandates the establishment of a Tribes Advisory Council (TAC) consisting of up to 20 members (three-fourths of whom must be ST MLAs).

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA), 1996 mandates that the Gram Sabha must be consulted prior to acquiring land in Scheduled Areas for development projects.
Reason (R): PESA was enacted to restore traditional tribal self-governance and protect indigenous communities against alienation of their land and forest resources.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Both statements are completely true and (R) provides the core legislative purpose behind the mandatory Gram Sabha consultation mandated by PESA 1996.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match List-I (Tribe) with List-II (Linguistic Family):
List-I:
(P) Santhal
(Q) Gond
(R) Garo
(S) Bhil

List-II:
(1) Dravidian
(2) Austro-Asiatic (Munda)
(3) Indo-Aryan
(4) Tibeto-Burman
practiceQuestions.explanation: Santhal = Austro-Asiatic (Munda); Gond = Dravidian (Gondi); Garo = Tibeto-Burman; Bhil = Indo-Aryan (Bhili).

practiceQuestions.question: How many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) have been officially recognized across India based on the criteria formulated by the Dhebar Commission?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Government of India has identified 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) spread across 18 States and the Union Territory of Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

practiceQuestions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act bifurcated the National Commission for SCs and STs, establishing a dedicated independent National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 established a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) under Article 338A.

practiceQuestions.question: Which nomadic hunter-gatherer tribal group of Jharkhand is famously noted in anthropology for their specialized traditional livelihood of making wooden mortars and cordage?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Birhor (literally 'men of the forest') are a semi-nomadic foraging PVTG of Jharkhand specializing in monkey-trapping, bark-rope twisting, and wooden crafts.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following states is NOT among the four states administered under the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule applies exclusively to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram (AMTM). Nagaland is governed by Article 371A rather than the Sixth Schedule.

practiceQuestions.question: The historic Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act was passed by the Indian Parliament in which year?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Forest Rights Act (FRA) was passed in 2006 to rectify the historical injustice done to forest-dwelling tribal communities by recognizing individual and community forest land rights.
